versionLinkTitle: View the latest release and downloads
maxRulesReached: Rule limit reached ($1 rules max). Delete some rules first
noRulesHint: Add a rule to start proxying cross-origin requests
guideImportDesc: Import an existing config from JSON
targetUrlHint: Leave empty to forward the original URL unchanged — for header/parameter injection only, or to bypass page CORS
derivedSameTargetHint: The target and the matched origin are the same address, so this rule won't rewrite any request. That's intentional if you only inject headers or parameters — to switch environments, point the target at the other environment's address.
targetCandidatePlaceholder: Pick one, or paste a new address
regexRefCountNone: The pattern has no capture group
regexRefOk: resolves — both channels will substitute this segment
regexRefWholeMatch: means the whole matched URL, not a capture group
regexRefOutOfRange: is out of range: the pattern only has $1 capture group(s). The network layer rejects the rule; the forwarding channel leaves this reference in the URL as-is
regexRefNoGroupAtAll: is out of range: the pattern has no capture group at all. The network layer rejects the rule; the forwarding channel leaves this reference in the URL as-is
regexRefBeyondNine: is above 9: the forwarding channel can reach this group, but the network layer reads one digit at a time and sees group 1 followed by a digit
regexRefUnused: The target URL references no capture group: the matched segment is replaced by this address wholesale, the path is not carried over
regexSummaryOk: References line up with the capture groups
regexSummaryRejected: A reference is out of range or above 9, so the browser's network layer would reject this substitution (the cost is the whole batch of rules failing to apply)
regexRefSyntaxNote: In regex mode, $1 and $2 in the target URL refer to the captured text; the network layer spells them \1 and \2 and the extension converts on save
regexRefChannelNote: The two channels rewrite different spans: the network layer uses the substitution as the entire new URL, while the forwarding channel replaces only the matched segment
invalidRequestHeader: Invalid request header(s), fix them before saving: $1 (names allow letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~; values must not contain line breaks)
invalidResponseHeader: Invalid response header(s), fix them before saving: $1 (names allow letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~; values must not contain line breaks)
duplicateOverrideNames: Duplicate name(s) — only the last entry per name takes effect: $1
logsReadStale: Below are the last records that came through
exportDesc: Export all proxy rules as a JSON file
exportSanitizeLabel: Share mode: strip credentials from headers and query params
exportSanitizeTip: Strips Authorization, Cookie and similar request/response headers from both the config file and the HAR; the config export additionally drops token-like query-parameter overrides, while the HAR keeps bodies and URLs as captured so the recording still reproduces the problem. The result is safe to share — untick for a complete local backup.
importDesc: Import config from a JSON file; "Replace" swaps the whole rule set, and you can preview the counts before importing
selectFileOrPaste: Select a file or paste JSON config
confirmImport: Importing will overwrite existing rules. Continue?
importSuccessDetail: Import finished: $1 added, $2 duplicates skipped, $3 invalid entries dropped
importSchemaTooNew: This file was exported by a newer version of the extension and can't be read fully — import rejected
importPreviewSkipped: $1 share a name and match pattern with existing rules and will be skipped (merge never updates existing rules)
importPreviewReplaces: The current $1 rules will be replaced wholesale; the rules being replaced are kept as a restore point
importPreviewDuplicates: $1 entries duplicate each other inside the file and will all be written (dedup only compares against existing rules)
importPreviewConflictItem: "$1" already exists: keeping $2, the file's $3 will not take effect
importPreviewConflictMore: $1 more conflicts of this kind not shown
importPreviewConflictHint: To change a target URL, edit the existing rule after importing, or delete it first
importPreviewExceedsLimit: Above the $1-rule limit — this import is expected to be rejected as a whole
importPreviewFailed: Preview unavailable, you can still import (the result message is authoritative)
filterNoMatch: No rules match the current filters
noMatch: Rule does not match this URL
readFailed: Saved rules can't be read right now, possibly because the background is restarting. It recovers on its own, or you can refresh manually.
dnrStatsHint: Rules that only rewrite the URL are redirected by the browser's network layer and produce no per-request logs; this is a rule-level hit count over a rolling 5-minute window. Use the URL match tester to confirm which channel a given URL takes, and note that refreshing too often can exhaust the query quota — the counts then still come from the previous query
dnrStatsEmpty: No DNR hits in the last 5 minutes
templateDesc: Click a template to quickly create a rule with pre-filled settings
wildcardApiProxyDesc: Redirect all requests from one domain to another using wildcards
prefixPathProxyDesc: Redirect API paths across domains, e.g. v1 → v2
addAuthHeaderDesc: Inject an Authorization: Bearer header into matched requests
customHeaderOverrideDesc: Override specific request headers for matched URLs
mockApiResponseDesc: Return a canned response body for matched requests instead of waiting on the backend
simulateSlowNetworkDesc: Add a 3s delay to matched requests to exercise loading and timeout handling
blockRequestDesc: Make matched requests fail like a network error to exercise your error branches
undoExpired: Undo window closed — the rule has been deleted
batchUndoExpired: Undo window closed — those $1 rule(s) have been deleted
deleteUndoFailed: The delete could not be saved — the rule is back in the list
requestBodyOverridePlaceholder: Enter request body to override original (e.g. JSON)
responseStatusTextStripped: Those characters cannot go on the wire — the browser will receive
responseBodyRawPlaceholder: Enter the full response body to replace everything upstream returned
responseBodyRawHint: Replaces the whole response body as-is, with no JSON parsing; leave empty to keep upstream's body
responseBodyRawShadowsReplacements: Whole-body replacement wins: the JSON field replacements below don't run right now — clear this box to go back to per-field replacement
exportHarDesc: Export captured request/response logs as HAR format
exportHarRedacted: Share mode is on: the HAR drops credential headers such as Authorization and Cookie (bodies unchanged).
exportHarFull: Share mode is off: the HAR is written exactly as captured, including real site headers. Do not forward it as-is.
importHarDesc: Import a HAR file to create one proxy rule per captured origin. Set a target environment to point them all in one go; leave it empty and the rules arrive self-mapping and disabled, until you edit each target.
importHarTargetDesc: If set, every rule from this capture points at it. Only the scheme, host and port are used, so pasting a full URL is fine.
importHarTargetInvalid: No http(s) origin found — this import will create self-mapping rules as before.
importHarRelocateCredentialsDesc: When on, the raw Authorization / Cookie / x-api-key values in the HAR move to Settings → Credential Variables and the rules keep only {{NAME}} references; headers that no longer fit the variable table, or whose value exceeds the per-entry length limit, keep their captured values and the toast names how many. Leave it off for the previous behaviour, where the raw value goes straight into the rule.
importHarSuccessRelocated: ; $1 credential header(s) now use a variable reference
importHarSuccessKeptRaw: ; $1 credential header(s) kept verbatim (table full or value too long)
importHarSuccessWithTarget: Created $1 rule(s) from HAR, all pointing at $2
importHarMultiOriginTitle: Point multiple origins at one environment?
importHarMultiOriginConfirm: This HAR contains $1 distinct origins. Setting a target environment rewrites all of them to one address, and captured credential headers will travel with those requests. Origins include: $2. Continue?
fileReadFailed: Could not read the file, please pick it again
fileTooLarge: This file is $1, over the $2 limit — trim it down and import again
importHarTooManyEntries: This HAR has $1 entries, over the $2-entry import limit — trim it down and import again
importOpenApiDesc: Pick an API document (OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2, as JSON) and create one proxy rule per server it declares. Set a target environment to point them all in one go; leave it empty and the rules arrive self-mapping and disabled, until you edit each target.
importOpenApiTip: JSON only; convert YAML to JSON first
importOpenApiSuccessWithTarget: Created $1 rule(s) from the document, all pointing at $2
importOpenApiSkipped: ; $1 source(s) had no readable http(s) address and were skipped
importOpenApiNotJson: Not JSON — convert an OpenAPI YAML document to JSON first
importOpenApiUnsupported: This is not an OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 document: no version marker, or no paths
importOpenApiNoServers: This document declares no usable servers / host address
detailNoData: No detail data captured for this request
detailBodyBinary: Binary response bodies are not stored in the local log — text responses only
mockBodyPlaceholder: Enter mock response body (JSON, text, etc.)
mockIgnored: Mock is enabled but body, status and conditions are all empty — Mock won't be saved
swStatsHint: Hit counts for rules processed by the Service Worker channel (recounted from zero after a config change or when the service worker is recycled)
confirmImportMerge: Merge will add non-duplicate rules from the import. Continue?
wsRuleHint: Also applies to WebSocket: only URL rewrite, query parameters and blocking take effect; header/body/response overrides, mock, delay, retry and sending cookies do not apply to sockets
hitStatsNetNotApplicable: This rule is proxied by the extension channel, not the network layer
hitStatsExtTip: Extension-channel (SW) hits: since the last config change or worker restart
hitStatsExtNotApplicable: This rule redirects at the network layer, not through the extension channel
conflictWarningMsg: This rule has the same match pattern as rule "$1" which has higher priority. This rule may never fire.
dnrSkippedIntro: This rule goes through the DNR channel, but Chrome will not apply it.
dnrSkippedRe2: The regex uses syntax RE2 does not support (lookaround, backreferences).
dnrSkippedSubstitution: The target URL's capture-group reference cannot be applied (out of range, or above 9).
dnrSkippedHint: Switch to wildcard or prefix matching, or give the rule a SW-only capability (method filter, header override, ...) so it runs through the proxy channel instead.
dnrSkippedSummary: $1 of them will not be applied by Chrome
dnrSkippedMsg: Rule saved, but Chrome will not apply it: $1
profilesDesc: Save the current rule set as a named snapshot and switch between environments (e.g. FAT / UAT / PROD) with one click.
profilesNoRulesHint: There are no rules to save
profilesEmptyHint: Save your current rules as a snapshot to switch between environments quickly
profileDamaged: This snapshot is damaged and cannot be loaded; you can delete it
confirmLoadProfile: Loading "$1" will REPLACE the current rule set ($2 rules) and turn the proxy switch on. Your current config is saved first as a restore point. Continue?
autoOffHint: Automatically turns the proxy off after the set duration while enabled, preventing forgotten proxy sessions
variablesHint: Write tokens and other secrets in your rules as {{NAME}} to reference variables stored here: the real values live in one local place and never leave through an exported config file or a page-side script.
variablesOrphanWarning: Rules reference variables that no longer exist: $1
variableNameInvalid: Names must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen — up to 64 characters
variablesDropped: $1 variable(s) were ignored for an invalid name or length — fix them and try again
variablesLoadFailed: Couldn't load credential variables — the list below is not the current state.
variablesWriteBlocked: Credential variables couldn't be read, so this overwrite was blocked (it would wipe the stored ones). Try loading them again.
confirmDeleteVariable: $1 rule(s) currently reference it. After deletion those requests send the literal {{NAME}} and will most likely fail. Delete anyway?
undefinedVariableError: The rule references undefined variables: $1. Create them under Settings → Credential Variables, or fix the reference.
variableWsQueryUnsupportedError: Query parameters of a WebSocket rule are built page-side, which cannot read the variable store — {{NAME}} references are not supported there.
headerOverridesHint: Values may reference credentials stored under Settings → Credential Variables as {{NAME}}, so exporting or sharing the config never carries the real value.
variableInsertLabel: Click to append to the last focused row:
variableLoadFailedHint: Couldn't read credential variables this time. Reopen the form to try again.
variableEmptyHint: No credential variables yet — add them under Settings → Credential Variables, then reference them here as {{NAME}}.
restorePointsHint: Operations that replace the whole rule set (replace-mode import, loading a profile, a batch delete that actually removed something) record the config they replace locally, keeping up to $1 of them. Use them here to undo a bad import
restorePointsLoadFailed: Couldn't load restore points — reopen this dialog
restoreConfirm: This replaces the current rule set with the snapshot ($1 rules). The global proxy switch stays as it is, and the current config is recorded as a restore point. Continue?
mockFromLogNoBody: This entry has no response body (it failed, was blocked, or went out through the network layer), so it can't become a Mock.
mockFromLogNoStatus: This entry has no status code, so it can't become a Mock.
mockFromLogBase64: This is a binary response — stored as a text Mock it would deliver a broken response, so it isn't offered.
mockFromLogTruncated: The body was truncated when it was logged; half a JSON only moves the error into the page's JSON.parse, so it isn't offered.
mockFromLogBadUrl: This entry's address has no readable http(s) origin, so it can't become a Mock.
mockFromLogQueryNote: The Mock matches by path: any query string on the same path receives this response.
mockFromLogScopeNote: Mocks run through the extension's background channel, so they apply to the page's own fetch / XHR only — image and script requests are unaffected.
mockFromLogBodyNote: The response body is stored in the rule as-is; share mode strips credential headers on export, never the body.
selfCheckRowsReading: Reading these five checks (global switch, this site, config delivery, match and channel, network-layer install); no conclusion before they land.
selfCheckRowsRefreshing: The five rows below are from the previous check - this round is still in flight.
selfCheckNoTab: Three of the rows below ask about _that page_; there is no web page here, so they will honestly stay at "unknown".
selfCheckFootnote: Every row asks a predicate already computed elsewhere; this panel keeps no second model of what the proxy would do, and "unknown" is never drawn as "fine".
selfCheckSwitchOk: The proxy switch is on with $1 rules enabled.
selfCheckSwitchOff: The proxy switch is off - nothing gets rewritten right now.
selfCheckSwitchUnknown: The global proxy switch could not be read, so this row draws no conclusion - it is neither "on" nor "off".
selfCheckSiteOk: This site is inside the proxy scope ($1).
selfCheckSiteBlocked: This site is outside the proxy scope ($1); neither channel touches it.
selfCheckSiteUnknown: The site scope or that page's host could not be read, so this row draws no conclusion.
selfCheckDeliveryOk: Nothing is on record about this page missing the latest config push - the ledger only records known misses, so this says "no record", not "confirmed received".
selfCheckDeliveryStale: This page has not received the latest config push - complex rules go live through it; reloading the page usually fixes it.
selfCheckDeliveryUnknown: The delivery ledger could not be read, or there is no web page to ask about.
selfCheckMatchPending: This page's address matches "$1", via $2; whether Chrome will apply that rule has not settled this round, so this row draws no conclusion on it.
selfCheckMatchNone: No enabled rule covers this page's address.
selfCheckMatchSkipped: The matching rule "$1" is one Chrome will never install (unsupported RE2 syntax or an out-of-range capture reference); the rule list's "Not applied" badge says which and why.
selfCheckMatchUnknown: Neither the rule set nor the page address could be read, so this row draws no conclusion.
selfCheckInstallOk: $1 redirect rules are installed in the network layer, matching what this config should install.
selfCheckInstallPending: $1 redirect rules are installed and this config should install $2 - a sync is still queued, so a difference at that moment is not a conclusion.
selfCheckInstallUnknown: The network-layer install state could not be read, so this row draws no conclusion.
selfCheckInstallMismatch: $1 rules are installed but this config should install $2 - the two disagree. When the ones that should be installed are missing, the usual cause is the last sync being rejected as a batch (one invalid item is enough); check the "Not applied" badge in the rule list.
selfCheckUnknown: This row could not be read, so it draws no conclusion.
replayConfirmBody: This replays $1 $2 through whatever the rules say right now. On a non-idempotent endpoint that can mean submitting it twice.
replayNoAnswer: No answer came back for this one (the background may have just been recycled). Try again.
replayAnswered: It went out under the current rules — the status above is what the server said this time.
replayMock: The matched rule has a Mock, so nothing left the machine: that response is the fake body from the rule.
replayBlocked: The matched rule blocks this request, so it was never sent.
replayNoRule: No enabled rule matches that address and method any more, so nothing was proxied.
replaySiteExcluded: A replay starts from the extension's own page, so there is no initiating host to judge — under "only sites in the list" scope the proxy leaves it alone.
replayDisabled: The proxy is switched off, so nothing was proxied.
replayInvalidRuleHeaders: The matched rule contains an invalid header name, so the proxy refused to send it.
replayRequestTooLarge: The body is over the proxy's size limit, so it was not sent (and never sent truncated either). The line below says what that limit is.
replayResponseTooLarge: The server answered, but its body went over the proxy's size limit and was cut off — this body is not complete. The line below says what that limit is.
replayFailed: This one did not complete: a timeout, an offline network, a DNS failure and a refused connection all look the same here. The exact words are below.
replayNoHeaders: This entry kept no request headers, so only the method, address and body went out — it is not the same request.
replayBinaryBody: The response is binary, so its body is not shown here.
replayBodyTruncated: Shown only for display: the first $1 characters of a $2-character body.
replayRefuseTruncated: A field in this entry was truncated when it was logged (the marker is still in the text). Sending it as-is would put a broken address or body on the wire together with the original credentials, so this one cannot be replayed.
replayRefuseUnusable: This entry is missing a field needed to send it (the address or method cannot be read), so there is no replay for it.
createRuleFromLogFailed: Failed to create rule: cannot parse request URL
importCurlDesc: Paste a cURL command (e.g. DevTools "Copy as cURL") to prefill a rule automatically
importCurlSuccess: cURL parsed. Confirm and save in the rule form
importCurlFailed: Failed to parse cURL: no valid request found
urlTestPlaceholder: Enter a URL to preview match results in real time
urlTestHint: Enter a URL to see the matched rule, rewritten URL and forwarding channel in real time
urlTestProxyOff: Proxy is disabled, rules will not take effect
urlTestNoMatchDesc: This URL will not be rewritten and will be sent as-is
urlTestCorsNote: DNR only rewrites the request URL at the network layer — the response never passes through the extension, so Chrome still enforces CORS: if the target environment doesn't return a matching Access-Control-Allow-Origin, the request is blocked. Add any advanced capability (header override, method filter, mock, ...) and the rule switches to extension-side fetching, which is exempt from CORS.
urlTestDivergenceTitle: This regex yields two different URLs on the two paths
urlTestDivergenceHint: When the pattern does not cover the whole URL, the network layer rebuilds the entire address from the substitution template while the extension replaces only the matched fragment. Anchor the pattern so it covers the whole URL (e.g. ^https://fat.com/api/(.*)$), or switch to wildcard / prefix matching — those two behave the same on both paths.
urlTestShadowedTitle: Also matched but shadowed by the rule above:
methodsHint: Proxy only these HTTP methods. Leave empty to match any. Setting methods routes the rule through the Service Worker.
tagsPlaceholder: Type and press Enter; pick an existing tag or add a new one
tagsHint: Classification only — tags change neither matching nor routing. $1 used of $2.
tagsDropped: $1 tag(s) were cleaned (over the length or count limit, duplicate, blank, or a reserved name); the rule was saved with the rest.
queryOverridesHint: Append or override query parameters on the final proxied URL (Service Worker channel). Values may reference a credential stored under Settings → Credential Variables as {{NAME}} (except on WebSocket rules).
sendCredentialsHint: Sends the target environment's cookies with proxied requests (Service Worker channel) so session-guarded endpoints work. Every request this rule matches then carries your login state there — enable it only for trusted environments.
migrateTargetsDesc: Replace part of the target URL across the selected rules (e.g. switch the target domain when environments rotate).
migrateFindPlaceholder: Text to find in target URL, e.g. uat-api.example.com
migrateNoSelection: Select at least one rule to migrate.
migrateNoMatch: No selected rule target contains the search text.
migrateFindRequired: Enter the text to find to preview changes.
logTableA11y: Request log list (use Up and Down arrows to pick a row, Enter to open details)
removeMockQueryParamA11y: Remove query parameter $1 from the conditional response
siteScopeListHint: Entries match by host including subdomains; scheme and port do not separate sites.
siteScopeLastWhitelistConfirm: Removing it leaves "Only listed sites" empty, and the current implementation falls back to "All sites", widening the proxy scope. Continue?
ratingDesc: The review page lives in the Chrome Web Store; clicking just takes you there. Nothing pops up on its own, nothing is blocked while you decide, and there is no reward to earn — this extension collects no usage data, so it never learns whether you clicked.
linksHint: The source, the guide and the issue tracker live at these addresses. Clicking just opens a tab: the extension makes no request because of it and never learns whether you clicked — there is no telemetry here.
